content.user_title: Analyze Research Data with Statistical Rigor
content.value_statement: Choosing and reporting statistical tests can be inconsistent and error-prone. This skill guides analysis planning, diagnostics, effect sizes, power, interpretation, and APA-style reporting.
actual_capabilities: Selects statistical tests from study design, variable types, and research questions.
Guides normality, variance, linearity, residual, and outlier diagnostics.
Explains t-tests, ANOVA, correlations, regression, chi-square tests, and nonparametric alternatives.
Supports Bayesian analysis planning, prior selection, convergence checks, and posterior interpretation.
Calculates and interprets effect sizes, confidence intervals, power, and sample size requirements.
Produces APA-style reporting guidance for methods, results, tables, and figures.
limitations: Users must provide accurate data, variable definitions, and study design details.
The skill does not replace review by a statistician or domain expert.
Python examples require compatible scientific libraries and a configured runtime.
Guidance cannot correct biased sampling, poor measurement, or invalid research design.

use_cases.title: Plan an Academic Study
use_cases.description: Choose tests, estimate sample size, define assumptions, and prepare a transparent analysis plan before data collection.

use_cases.title: Diagnose an Existing Model
use_cases.description: Review residuals, variance, normality, multicollinearity, and outliers before interpreting regression or group comparisons.

use_cases.title: Write Publication Results
use_cases.description: Convert statistical output into clear APA-style results with effect sizes, intervals, diagnostics, and appropriate limitations.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Statistical Test
prompt_templates.prompt: I have [outcome type], [groups or predictors], and [study design]. Recommend a test and explain the assumptions I should check.

prompt_templates.title: Check Analysis Assumptions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these variables and diagnostics: [details]. Identify violated assumptions, suitable remedies, and robust or nonparametric alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Power and Effect Sizes
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an analysis for [design] with expected effect [value], alpha [value], and power [value]. Estimate sample size and reporting requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Complete Analysis Strategy
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a preregistered analysis for [research question]. Include test selection, diagnostics, multiplicity controls, sensitivity checks, effect sizes, and APA reporting.

output_examples.input: Compare two independent groups on a continuous outcome with unequal variances.
output: Recommended test: Welch's independent samples t-test.
Check group distributions, influential outliers, independence, and measurement quality.
Report group summaries, t statistic, degrees of freedom, p-value, effect size, and confidence interval.

output_examples.input: Plan a multiple regression with three predictors and a continuous outcome.
output: Define the model before analysis and justify each predictor.
Check linearity, residual variance, residual normality, independence, influential observations, and multicollinearity.
Report model fit, coefficients, intervals, standardized effects, diagnostics, and sensitivity analyses.

output_examples.input: Rewrite a non-significant correlation result for an academic paper.
output_examples.output: The analysis found no statistically significant relationship. Report the coefficient, exact p-value, confidence interval, sample size, and detectable effect range.

best_practices: Provide the study design, variable types, sample sizes, missing-data details, and planned comparisons.
Share diagnostics and effect estimates instead of reporting only p-values.
Verify calculations and interpretations against the study protocol and relevant domain expertise.
anti_patterns: Do not select tests only because they produce a significant p-value.
Do not ignore assumptions, missing data, multiple comparisons, or influential observations.
Do not treat generated reporting text as final without validating the data and computations.

faq.question: Can this skill choose a statistical test?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the research question, variable types, group structure, repeated measures, and outcome distribution.

faq.question: Does it run analyses automatically?
faq.answer: It provides Python examples and a bundled assumption-checking module. Execution still requires a compatible local Python environment.

faq.question: Which statistical methods are covered?
faq.answer: It covers common t-tests, ANOVA, correlations, regression, chi-square tests, nonparametric alternatives, Bayesian methods, power, and effect sizes.

faq.question: Can it produce APA-style results?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides reporting of descriptive statistics, test statistics, p-values, effect sizes, intervals, assumptions, tables, and figures.

faq.question: Can it determine the required sample size?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the design, expected effect size, alpha level, desired power, allocation ratio, and planned test.

faq.question: Is this a substitute for a statistician?
faq.answer: No. Complex designs, high-stakes decisions, missing-data problems, and specialized models should receive expert review.
